title: The Devotions of Bishop Andrewes (Preces Privatae)
author: Lancelot Andrewes
tradition_notes: Lancelot Andrewes (1555–1626), Bishop of Winchester, wrote the Preces Privatae as a personal devotion book in Greek, Latin, and Hebrew. The Newman 1840 translation (Tract for the Times lxxviii) is the most accessible English version. Andrewes is the father of Caroline Anglicanism and one of the principal translators of the King James Bible.
source_edition: The Devotions of Bishop Andrewes. Vol. I. Translated by John Henry Newman (1840, Tract for the Times lxxviii). Edited by H. B. Swete. London: S.P.C.K., 1892.
notes: Newman's 1840 translation confirmed via preface signature 'J.H.N.' and Swete's introduction. Newman died 1890 (PD); Swete died 1917 (PD); 1892 edition pre-1928 (US PD). PG not confirmed; CCEL used for text quality. Vol. I only; CCEL does not appear to have Vol. II (Latin/Greek daily offices).
